name: hadavin-trigger-error (outline; earlier version run in n8n 2.47.7; this version not re-imported)

nodes.name: Error Trigger
nodes.notes: SEEN IN n8n 2.47.7: this node as written. This workflow ran once for every failed execution of the main workflow, but ONLY while it was published. Imported and not published, n8n logged that it 'is not active and cannot be executed' and nobody was told. So publishing this workflow is a required set-up step. One error workflow can serve many workflows; it is chosen in the main workflow's Workflow Settings.

nodes.name: Build message
nodes.notes: SEEN IN n8n 2.47.7: this node as written, with typeVersion 3.4: the message held the workflow name, the execution link, the last node and the error text. Keep typeVersion 3.4: with typeVersion 3 n8n ignored 'assignments' and the message was null. The four field paths used here were all in what the Error Trigger delivered. Do not add the request body or any header to the message, and do not pass on the whole error object: its field execution.error.node holds the failing node with all its parameters and notes. The message holds no key and no event: the person opens the execution (the link is in the message) to find which event it was. The message never holds the document text.

nodes.name: Notify placeholder
nodes.notes: UNVERIFIED: what lands here by design for a 520 to 524 answer and for the state check (a run that ended badly or still showed as running): none of that was ever run in n8n. SEEN IN n8n 2.47.7: this node as written (it does nothing). Replace it with the client's chat or e-mail node and send {{ $json.message }}. What lands here by design, because a person must look: a missing business id or document text; a 401, 409, 400 or 413 from the trigger endpoint (never tried again); and a 502, 503, 504, 520 to 524 or no answer in every round of the main workflow's wait-and-sign-again loop, which means: not acknowledged; send again with the same key; it may already be running. Also landing here by design, since the state check was added to the main workflow: a run that ended in a state that is not a success (NEEDS_PERSON, DENIED, REJECTED, EXPIRED, ROLLED_BACK or STOPPED; the message names the state, never a reason), and a run that still showed as running when the checks were used up. For a run that was cut off by a crash or a forced kill this message is the ONLY notice a person gets today: Hadavin itself tells nobody. A short restart of the Hadavin worker must NOT land here: the loop waits it out.
